summary: Agent passed all baseline and new tests with a legitimate reference-aware synthetic-retention implementation.

solution_quality.reasoning: The agent added the disabled-by-default preference and implemented a production fixed-point render/scan loop over semantic TextBuffer tokens. It makes per-field, per-method/bridge, and per-member-class decisions, excludes declaration tokens and non-code text, handles transitive references, and preserves the disabled path. The agent's added tests and fixtures are normal regression coverage; it did not modify or know the hidden verifier, and its implementation differs materially from the human reference solution.

problem_assessment.notes: The prompt explicitly defines scope, option default, reconstruction-dependent behavior, code-versus-text references, file-wide reachability, per-member minimality, and determinism. The hidden tests exercise all of those requirements by recompiling emitted Java and checking behavior and declaration sets. The task is substantial but fair, and the reference solution confirms feasibility.

evidence: The verifier wrapper completed successfully and reported 17 tests passed, including 3 baseline and 13 new JUnit test cases.
The trajectory shows unusually long Gradle compilation/test waits, but those commands eventually completed and the agent also ran a direct compiled JUnit check with all 7 targeted tests passing.
No dependency, permission, runtime, bootstrap, API, or hidden-verifier failure prevented implementation or validation.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; slow local Gradle execution did not prevent successful validation.
